== Course of events ==

After being freed from his long rust by having his joints oiled, the Scarecrow's companion realizes the toll his years of immobility have taken: he has lost his ability to love the Munchkin girl he once wanted to marry. This loss leads him to conclude that happiness cannot exist without a heart, since without one he can no longer feel affection for her. The Scarecrow, hearing this view, disagrees, maintaining instead that brains matter more than a heart when it comes to living well.

The disagreement between the two is not resolved on the road; each continues to hold his own conviction, one prizing feeling and the other prizing intellect. This unresolved difference sets the stage for what follows, as the character who lost his love resolves to ask Oz for a heart, mirroring the Scarecrow's own wish to ask Oz for brains.
